account: Catherine Tan Li Eng, 51, took 19 Jacob's Creek wine bottles worth about S$556 from the Sheng Siong supermarket at Block 622D Punggol Central, Singapore. She bagged them unscanned at self-checkout from 2 to 11 September 2025. On 10 September staff found stock discrepancies, reviewed closed-circuit television (CCTV) and uploaded her face to the chain's AI-driven facial recognition system. It automatically identified the earlier thefts. When she returned at noon on 11 September the retail manager got a phone alert. He stopped her at the self-checkout kiosk and found three unscanned bottles. Police arrested her. The Straits Times reports that the alert and the interception happened at noon on 11 September 2025. A similar case followed at the chain's Sin Ming Avenue outlet, where the system alerted staff on 1 October 2025 to a woman who had stolen on 12 visits. On 12 May 2026 District Judge Brenda Chua jailed Tan for eight days on an amalgamated theft charge after full restitution of about S$470. The woman caught at the Sin Ming Avenue outlet was jailed for one week on 8 October 2026.

ai_role.statement: The system's documented contribution came after a human detection. On 10 September 2025 a staff member found discrepancies in a stock check. Colleagues reviewed CCTV and saw Tan leaving without paying. They uploaded her face. The Straits Times reports that the system “then automatically identified the other instances” of theft. That turned one observed theft into an amalgamated charge covering seven visits. On 11 September the system's alert reached the retail manager's phone when she entered. He intercepted her at the self-checkout kiosk with three unscanned bottles. The interception, the bag check, the police call, the prosecution and the restitution were human and institutional. No source names the vendor or the model, gives an accuracy figure, or reports a false match in this case.

fields.purpose: Sheng Siong rolled out its AI-driven facial recognition CCTV system in April 2024 as a measure against shoplifters. It worked with the Singapore Police Force under its Shop Theft for Retailers (STAR) program. In August 2025 it announced an extension to all 83 outlets. Staff upload the photograph of a suspect identified from footage. The system alerts store managers' phones when that person enters any branch. Sheng Siong said that thefts per store rose from 4.91 in 2023 to 8 in 2024. Its CEO attributed the rise to catching cases that the human eye had missed. The system was designed to identify repeat shoplifters and flag their return.

fields.account: Catherine Tan Li Eng, 51, took 19 Jacob's Creek wine bottles worth about S$556 from the Sheng Siong supermarket at Block 622D Punggol Central, Singapore. She bagged them unscanned at self-checkout from 2 to 11 September 2025. On 10 September staff found stock discrepancies, reviewed closed-circuit television (CCTV) and uploaded her face to the chain's AI-driven facial recognition system. It automatically identified the earlier thefts. When she returned at noon on 11 September the retail manager got a phone alert. He stopped her at the self-checkout kiosk and found three unscanned bottles. Police arrested her. The Straits Times reports that the alert and the interception happened at noon on 11 September 2025. A similar case followed at the chain's Sin Ming Avenue outlet, where the system alerted staff on 1 October 2025 to a woman who had stolen on 12 visits. On 12 May 2026 District Judge Brenda Chua jailed Tan for eight days on an amalgamated theft charge after full restitution of about S$470. The woman caught at the Sin Ming Avenue outlet was jailed for one week on 8 October 2026.

purpose: Sheng Siong rolled out its AI-driven facial recognition CCTV system in April 2024 as a measure against shoplifters. It worked with the Singapore Police Force under its Shop Theft for Retailers (STAR) program. In August 2025 it announced an extension to all 83 outlets. Staff upload the photograph of a suspect identified from footage. The system alerts store managers' phones when that person enters any branch. Sheng Siong said that thefts per store rose from 4.91 in 2023 to 8 in 2024. Its CEO attributed the rise to catching cases that the human eye had missed. The system was designed to identify repeat shoplifters and flag their return.
